identity: A childrens storybook from al-Maktaba al-Khadra li-l-Atfal: al-Malik Adil by Muhammad Atiyya al-Ibrashi, 13th printing - an Arabic retelling of Grimms King Thrushbeard. Four short front-matter lines (series, title, byline, edition) then ten narrative paragraphs. Median printed line 29.5 -> PROSE MODE for the body; the four front-matter lines are single catalogue fields already closed by <NL>.
law: Two regimes in one document. (1) Front matter: each field is its own unit (M1/M2/1g) - here each already occupies its own line, so nothing extra to do and no internal splitting of bi-qalam Muhammad Atiyya al-Ibrashi or al-tabaa al-thalitha ashara. (2) Narrative body: the unit is the orthographic SENTENCE, i.e. the deleted full stop (0p), which in this translators style is long - one main event with all its wa-/fa- continuations, its hal clauses and its masdar chains riding inside. Mean unit came out 22 tokens, inside the prose band. A cut is earned only by: a fronted time/place frame (cut BEFORE it, 0n/0x), a NEW AGENT taking over the action (0z.1), thumma opening a distinct new beat (0l), or a distinct enumerated item.
reasoning: The hard sites. (a) @95 wa-fi laylatin min al-layali and @389 wa-bada thalathati ayyam and @482 wa-bada an intaha - fronted temporal frames, so the boundary goes BEFORE them (0n/0x); at @481 that means the piper-plays clause ends and the after-he-finished clause opens, not the other way round. (b) The mockery list @154-@206: she says of the first, the second, the third... Items 3-6 (wa-an al-thalith / al-rabi / al-khamis / al-sadis) have NO verb of their own - they are PP conjuncts gapped on qalat - so under checklist v3 step 4 they are sub-clausal and merge into the qalat sentence; only the two verb-bearing sayings (fa-qalat an al-awwal, wa-qalat an al-thani) are separate sentences. I cut at @163 and then let @170/@176/@182/@189 ride. This is the split-vs-merge question of open contradiction #1 and I decided it on the presence of a repeated finite verb, not on parallelism. (c) @41 wa-lakinnaha kanat mutakabbira - I nearly cut here and did NOT. 0q demotes wa-lakin on three merges, and all three (qasr...wa-lakin nuqil, istaqala...wa-lakinnahu taraja, al-salama aliya lakin tujuhilat) keep the SAME subject; here the subject is still the princess and the topic is still her character, so it merges even though the resulting unit is 43 tokens. (d) @611 wa-lakin abaha lam yataaththar - the same particle, and here I DID cut, because the subject changes to the father and it is a counter-move in the plot, not a qualification of the same description. That is the discriminator I am extracting: wa-lakin + same subject merges, wa-lakin + new agent cuts. (e) @249 vs @254: the crowds laughter fa-dahika al-hadirun is the IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE of her mocking look, so by 1a it rides inside that beat and the period falls after it, before wa-qad taallama hadha al-malik al-shabb - a new agent. (f) @433 wa-huwa shabb zammar... is a hal description of the beggar already introduced, so A10 does not fire (0v: wa-huwa needs a NEW referent) and it merges. (g) Line 7 @300-@334 has three coordinated finite verbs about one reaction (taallama / ghadiba / khajila) plus a seven-member masdar chain - 1d and 0t both say merge, so 35 tokens is ONE unit with no internal cut. (h) Line 12 @521-@538, the musician rejoiced / the princess was pained, is a matched contrast pair = one record (0m), so no cut despite the agent change; the whole paragraph is 18 tokens, already a normal unit. (i) The two speeches @494-@519 and @540-@595 are segmented as prose (a long speech is not one blob, 0k/1e): the king praises, then announces the reward after a fronted causal PP; then he states the vow, identifies the piper, and restates the obligation.
